catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-enge: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey of Engelberg — the mountain of angels in the Swiss Alps — traces its Benedictine history. George Cyprian Alston gives the full account. A lofty reference on an Alpine abbey. Its cheese and its choir both enjoy a wide fame.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adolphus-von-: A 1913 entry on Adolphus von Dalberg — the prince-abbot of Fulda. Michael Ott notes his baroque age. His abbey shone with imperial splendor. Mitre and sword met in his person. A prince of the old Empire. His university at Fulda spread the Enlightenment.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albert-of-bra: A 1913 entry on Albert of Brandenburg — the archbishop of the indulgence storm. Miles O'Malia tells his splendid, troubled career. Tetzel preached at his commission. Luther's hammer answered his pomp. A prince of the Church at the Reformation's dawn. His tomb in Mainz shows his pride.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-augsburg: A 1913 entry on Augsburg — the Bavarian diocese of the Confession's city. Joseph Lins tells its storied past. The diet of 1530 split the faith. Its bishops date from antiquity. The city of the famous Confession. Its Fuggerei is the poor's haven.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bamberg: This 1913 reference piece on Bamberg — the see Henry the Saint founded — honors its past. Joseph Lins wrote it up. Its church crowns the Franconian hills. The emperor sleeps in its choir. A prince-bishopric of the old Reich. Its stone horseman guards the nave.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baron-joseph-: A 1913 entry on Joseph von Lassberg — the collector of German manuscripts. Arthur Remy notes his antiquarian zeal. His castle library held the Nibelungen. The scholars bless his hoard. A baron among the bookmen. His Meersburg castle held the books. His Liederhort gathered the folk songs.
